title: How to Bake Sourdough Savory Waffles in the Oven
meta_description: Learn how to bake sourdough savory waffles in the oven with step‑by‑step instructions, tips for perfect texture, and why silicone baking mats are a game‑changer
html:
If you’ve ever wanted the crisp‑on‑the‑outside, fluffy‑inside bite of a waffle without turning on the waffle iron, oven baked sourdough waffles are the answer. Using a sourdough starter adds depth and a slight tang that pairs beautifully with savory add‑ins like cheese, herbs, and bacon. This guide walks you through the entire process—from feeding your starter to achieving golden edges on a sheet pan—while showing how a silicone baking mat can replace parchment for a flawless release and zero‑scrub cleanup.

Why Choose Oven‑Baked Sourdough Waffles?

Traditional waffle irons require a lot of preheating time and constant flipping, and they’re limited to one batch at a time. Baking the waffles in the oven lets you produce a larger quantity on a single sheet, perfect for brunch crowds or meal‑prep. The sourdough starter contributes natural leavening, which means the waffles rise without extra baking powder, and the fermentation process adds a subtle sour note that balances salty cheeses or spicy peppers.

Gather Your Ingredients and Tools

Having everything ready makes the process smooth and helps you avoid over‑mixing, which can toughen the batter. Below is a basic list; feel free to customize the savory mix‑ins to suit your palate.

  1. 1 cup active sourdough starter (fed and bubbly)
  2. 1 cup all‑purpose flour
  3. ½ cup whole‑milk yogurt or buttermilk
  4. 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  5. ¼ cup melted butter, plus extra for greasing
  6. ½ teaspoon salt
  7. ½ teaspoon garlic powder
  8. ¼ teaspoon black pepper
  9. 1 cup shredded sharp cheddar (or your favorite cheese)
  10. ¼ cup chopped fresh herbs (chives, parsley, or thyme)
  11. Optional add‑ins: cooked bacon bits, diced jalapeños, or caramelized onions
  12. Silicone Baking Mats – non‑stick, reusable mats that replace parchment for even baking and zero‑scrub cleanup.

Step‑by‑Step: Baking the Waffles

1. Preheat the oven. Set it to 425°F (220°C). A hot oven creates the steam needed for a crisp exterior while the interior stays tender.

2. Prepare the sheet pan. Lay a silicone baking mat on a rimmed baking sheet. The mat’s non‑stick surface eliminates the need for parchment and makes cleanup a breeze.

3. Mix the wet ingredients. In a medium bowl, whisk together the sourdough starter, yogurt, eggs, and melted butter until smooth.

4. Combine the dry ingredients. In a separate bowl, sift the flour, salt, garlic powder, and black pepper. Sifting prevents lumps and ensures an even rise.

5. Bring it together. Fold the dry mixture into the wet mixture just until incorporated. Over‑mixing can develop gluten, leading to dense waffles. The batter should be slightly thick but pourable.

6. Add the savory extras. Gently fold in the cheese, herbs, and any optional add‑ins. The cheese will melt into pockets, giving each bite a gooey center.

7. Shape the waffles. Using a ¼‑cup measuring cup, drop batter onto the silicone mat, spacing each mound about 2 inches apart. For a uniform look, you can use a small cookie scoop.

8. Bake. Place the sheet in the preheated oven and bake for 12‑15 minutes, or until the edges turn golden brown and the tops are set. If you like extra crunch, switch the oven to broil for the last minute—watch closely to avoid burning.

9. Cool and serve. Let the waffles rest on the mat for 2 minutes before sliding them onto a wire rack. This short rest lets steam escape, preserving the crisp crust.

Tips for Perfect Texture and Flavor

  • Use a well‑fed starter. A starter that’s been fed within the last 12 hours will be most active, giving the waffles lift without the need for chemical leaveners.
  • Don’t over‑mix. Stop stirring once the flour is just incorporated. A few lumps are fine; they’ll hydrate during baking.
  • Choose the right cheese. Sharp cheeses like cheddar or Gruyère melt well and add a robust flavor that stands up to the sour notes.
  • Season after baking. A light drizzle of melted butter or a sprinkle of flaky sea salt right after the waffles come out of the oven adds a finishing touch.
  • Reuse the silicone mat. After the batch cools, simply wipe the mat with a damp cloth. No parchment waste, no scrubbing—just a quick rinse and it’s ready for the next round.

Storing and Reheating

Leftover waffles keep well in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to three days. To reheat, spread them on a baking sheet lined with a silicone baking mat and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 5‑7 minutes. The mat prevents sticking and helps retain the original crispness without additional oil.

FAQ

Can I use a regular baking sheet without a silicone mat?

Yes, but a silicone baking mat provides a truly non‑stick surface, eliminates the need for parchment, and makes cleanup effortless. It also distributes heat evenly, which helps the waffles brown uniformly.

What if I don’t have a sourdough starter?

You can substitute 1 cup of buttermilk and 1 teaspoon of baking powder for the starter, but you’ll lose the distinctive tang and natural leavening that make these waffles special.

Can I freeze the baked waffles?

Absolutely. Once cooled, arrange the waffles in a single layer on a baking sheet, freeze until solid, then transfer to a freezer‑safe bag. Reheat directly from frozen on a preheated sheet with a silicone mat for 8‑10 minutes.
